[32933 Research Project | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This subject equips you with practical research skills, enabling you to tackle novel problems using ICT technologies through individual or small team projects, guided by academic staff and senior researchers. You'll develop critical thinking, problem-solving, and effective communication abilities, assessed via research quality, written reports, and oral presentations. Your learning journey is self-directed, with support from a dedicated supervisor and subject coordinator, and while there are no formal classes, you're expected to proactively schedule regular supervisory meetings. An introductory guide will be available on Canvas.

[32933 Research Project | Learning and teaching activities]
The subject is independent and self-motivated work by the participant, assisted by the participant's individual project supervisor and the subject coordinator.

 There are no formal classes, but students should meet regularly with their supervisor. Students are responsible for organising regular meetings. An introduction to the subject will be posted on Canvas.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[32933 Research Project | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Conceptualise, design, plan, and implement research studies in their field of study and practice. (C.1)
SLO2: Apply at least one research method applicable to ICT fields. (C.1)
SLO3: Write a research report in appropriate format and style, including the research background, design, implementation, results and conclusions. (E.1)
SLO4: Give an oral presentation on the research background, design, implementation, results and conclusions to an audience of peers and staff. (E.1)
SLO5: Conduct critical self and peer assessments. (F.1)

[32933 Research Project | Requisites]
Before you enrol in this subject, you must ensure you have met its requisites. The requisites for this subject can be viewed on its access conditions page. 

To learn more about requisites, please visit the How to use the Handbook guide.
